question.text: A cylinder of fixed capacity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>44</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn></math> litres contains helium gas at standard temperature and pressure. The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of gas in the cylinder by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> will be (Given gas constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
At STP volume occupied by one mole of a gas is 22.4 L. Therefore, number of moles are,  n=44.822.4=2 mol.

The process is isochoric process as the volume of the cylinder remains fixed and helium is a monatomic gas. Therefore, amount of heat needed will be,

Q=nCvΔT=232R20=3×8.3×20=498 J
